case_prompt: A 63-year-old woman underwent left knee replacement and was discharged on enoxaparin 40 mg subcutaneously once daily for thromboprophylaxis without planned platelet monitoring. Fifteen days later she presented with fever (39.5 °C), headache, acute right-sided weakness, and a 2-minute episode of altered consciousness with focal tremors in her right leg and abdomen. Noncontrast head CT was unremarkable. Brain MRI showed an acute infarct in the left precentral and postcentral gyri and a subacute infarct in the right parietal lobe. Laboratory studies revealed hemoglobin 10.6 g/dL, platelet count 43 000 × 10^9/L, and D-dimer 34 800 ηg/L; other values were within normal limits. She had no history of hypertension, diabetes, hyperlipidemia, smoking, or estrogen use. Physical examination noted right upper quadrant pain without hepatosplenomegaly or mucocutaneous bleeding. ECG demonstrated sinus rhythm, and echocardiography showed a nondilated left atrium with a normal ejection fraction (65%), excluding atrial fibrillation or intracardiac thrombus. Carotid duplex ultrasound was normal. CT pulmonary angiography revealed pulmonary emboli in the left main and segmental arteries. Abdominal CT identified filling defects in branches of the right suprahepatic vein. Venous ultrasound of the left leg showed nonacute thrombosis of the superficial femoral and popliteal veins. A repeat platelet count using citrate-anticoagulated blood confirmed thrombocytopenia.

diagnostic_reasoning: 1. Carotid atherosclerotic disease was ruled out because “the ultrasound of the supra-aortic trunks was also normal.” 2. Pseudothrombocytopenia, splenomegaly, and autoimmune thrombocytopenia were excluded, as supported by “the clinical suspicion of a HIT diagnosis was supported by… the exclusion of a thrombocytopenia due to splenomegaly, pseudothrombocytopenia, and autoimmune thrombocytopenia.”

selection.screen_reason: Thrombocytopenia with arterial and venous thromboses about two weeks after starting enoxaparin following knee replacement gives heparin-induced thrombocytopenia.
selection.second_look_note: Knee replacement with enoxaparin started 15 days earlier is the key history clue to thrombocytopenia with arterial and venous thromboses.
